argument.text: By H001, T>0 and 0<gamma<=1. For arbitrary real mean-zero g with ||g||_{H^gamma}<=R, reflection and sign give real mean-zero -g(-x) with the same Fourier norms. In particular its L2 and dot H^gamma norms are <=R. Instantiate E001 at s=gamma, b=T, B0=R and z0=-g(-x). Thus the equation U_t=U U_x+U_xxx admits a unique continuous dot H^gamma solution, and sup_{[0,T]}||U(t)||_{dot H^gamma}<=K_gamma(T,R,R), with K_gamma uniform over this ball. Smooth initial data belong to every positive integer Sobolev space; E001 at each such integer and uniqueness identify these regular solutions with the H^gamma solution, giving spatial smoothness. E001 at theta=0 and arbitrary two initial norms summing to at most B0 gives sup_{[0,T]}||U-Utilde||_2<=C(T,B0)||U(0)-Utilde(0)||_2. The source's dot H^gamma Lipschitz dependence also makes solutions of smooth Fourier approximations converge in C([0,T];dot H^gamma); coefficientwise norm comparison transfers this to H^gamma. The products converge in distributions since H^gamma convergence implies L2 convergence and squares then converge in L1.

produces.statement: For every real mean-zero g with ||g||_{H^gamma}<=R, there exists a unique C([0,T];dot H^gamma) solution of (Uflow)_t=Uflow (Uflow)_x+(Uflow)_xxx with Uflow(0,x)=-g(-x), with a finite uniform homogeneous norm bound depending only on T,gamma,R. For smooth initial g this solution is spatially smooth. For any two real mean-zero initial data in this class whose initial L2 norms sum to at most B0, their corresponding source-sign flows satisfy sup_{[0,T]}||Ufirst-Usecond||_2<=C(T,B0)||Ufirst(0)-Usecond(0)||_2. Smooth Fourier approximations converge to these flows in C([0,T];dot H^gamma), so their equations pass distributionally to the limit.

argument.text: Define \(u(t,x)=-U(t,-x)\). Then \(u_t=-U_t\), \(u_x=U_x\), \(u_{xxx}=U_{xxx}\) at \((t,-x)\), and consequently \(u_t+u_{xxx}=uu_x\). Fourier coefficients become \(\widehat u(k)=-\widehat U(-k)\), preserving every Sobolev norm, reality and zero mean. This transforms the source equation to u_t+u_xxx=(1/2)partial_x(u^2). The norm comparison above transfers all bounds to our \(H^\gamma\) norm. Hence there is \(A(T,\gamma,R)<\infty\) such that every smooth initial datum in the stated ball satisfies \(\sup_{[0,T]}\|u(t)\|_{H^\gamma}\le A\). The same bound holds for the limiting solution: for each finite set of frequencies pass to the limit in its finite norm sum, then take the supremum over finite sets. Thus \(M\le1+A(T,\gamma,R)\) uniformly. Continuous dependence in \(L^2\) is precisely the input used in the final density passage. No change of torus length or amplitude scaling is needed. More explicitly, the physical change u(t,x)=-U(t,-x) maps initial data g to source initial data -g(-x), so preserves the whole initial-data ball. The homogeneous-to-inhomogeneous inequalities follow coefficientwise from |k|<=<k><=sqrt(2)|k| for k!=0. For a continuous limiting flow the finite-frequency sums and then their supremum give the bound at each time, with the same constant. Apply the source pair bound after this isometry; it gives the stated C(T,B0) bound. Twisting by S_{-t} differentiates away -partial_x^3 and gives v'=B_t(v,v)/2. This proves all clauses of the output, for arbitrary data in the ball.

The weaker-norm pair conclusion is not used in this instance.

argument.text:
H001 supplies 0<gamma<=1 for the final numerical-state specialization. Independently fix lambda in [0,1], tau>0, step time t_n, and mean-zero polynomial inputs. Temporarily assume these range conditions as L1. Use the following computation with the proof's letter gamma replaced everywhere by lambda; no numerical state regularity is assumed.
 Only nonzero \(abck\) and \(p=a+b\ne0\) need consideration. Set \(k=a+b+c\), \(d=-k\), \(p=a+b\), \(A=|ab|\), \(B0=|ck|\), \(\alpha=3abp\), \(\beta=3kcp\), and write eta0=eta_tau(alpha,beta) as eta in this calculation. N002 and the first majorant in N002 give
\[
\frac{|\eta|}{|k|}\le\frac6{N_3}.
\]
For the other endpoint, observe that \(A B0=|abck|\), and use the linear phase bound in N002 and the second majorant in N002:
\[
\frac{|\eta|}{\tau|abck|}\le3\frac{|p|\min(A,B0)}{A B0}
=3\frac{|p|}{\max(A,B0)}\le\frac{18}{N_3}.
\]
Taking the geometric mean of these two bounds yields
\[
\boxed{\frac{|\eta_\tau(\alpha,\beta)|}{|k||abc|^\lambda}
\le\frac{6^{1-\lambda}18^\lambda\tau^\lambda}{N_3(a,b,c,-k)}.} 
\]



Dualize the remainder definition D014 against an \(\ell^2\) sequence and take absolute values. Apply N003 with \(x_1(a)=|a|^\lambda|\widehat f_1(a)|\) and analogously for \(x_2,x_3\); \(x_4(d)\) is the absolute value of the dual coefficient at \(-d\). Their norms are bounded by the inhomogeneous Sobolev norms and the dual norm. The factors \(e^{-it_n\Phi}\) have modulus one. The sum is bounded by C_lambda tau^(1+lambda) product_j||f_j||_{H^lambda}; deleting summands or multiplying them by scalars of modulus at most one preserves this absolute-value estimate. Polynomial approximation and the bound extend the operator to the claimed spaces. 
Here the two estimates used are directly N002 and the four-linear estimate is N003. At lambda=0 or 1 use the corresponding endpoint directly, so no 0^0 convention is needed.

produces.statement: For all lambda in [0,1], tau>0, real t_n and mean-zero polynomial f1,f2,f3, ||R^n_{2,tau}(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C_lambda tau^(1+lambda) product_{j=1}^3||f_j||_{H^lambda}, with constants independent of support and time. The same estimate holds after any summand restriction or insertion of multipliers of modulus <=1. For nonzero a,b,c,k=a+b+c with p=a+b!=0, alpha=3abp and beta=3kcp, |eta_tau(alpha,beta)|/(|k||abc|^lambda)<=6^(1-lambda)18^lambda tau^lambda/N3(a,b,c,-k).

argument.text:
The polynomial estimate F001 makes each Cauchy approximation converge in L2: expand a trilinear difference into three terms and apply the same bound. It gives a unique continuous trilinear extension to the mean-zero H^lambda completions and preserves the multiplier restrictions. For the numerical-state estimate fix mean-zero w in H^gamma, f in L2, ||w||_{H^gamma}<=M, delta=||f-w||_2<=1, and 0<tau<=1.  Apply F001 at lambda=gamma with exponent \(\gamma\) to \((w,w,w)\). Expand the difference between the cubic expressions at \(f\) and at \(w\), and apply F001 at lambda=0 to every difference term. This gives \(C\tau\delta(\|f\|_{L^2}+\|w\|_{L^2})^2\). No \(H^\gamma\) bound on the numerical state is used. 
Indeed ||f||_2<=M+1, so the difference is bounded by C_M tau delta, while the value at w is <=C M^3 tau^(1+gamma). These establish both assertions. Discharge L1 and the stated conditional specialization, retaining all its conditions in the output.

argument.text: Use H001. For E002 take arbitrary I=[a,b] with 0<=a<=b and b-a<=1 and lambda=0 for the X estimate. X gives precisely L-infinity L2 and L-infinity H^(-23/14) derivative, its hypotheses. Its three choices of negative-norm slot are retained. For constant inputs use E002 with any lambda in [0,1]. Each source spatial norm is sqrt(2 pi) times ours: divide by sqrt(2 pi) on the output and absorb the remaining product factors 2 pi into the constant. This proves the first two assertions without changing their exponent or time length. Smooth or continuous piecewise smooth time functions have the stated distributional derivative, so E002 applies directly. General X inputs use the source bounded interpretation of the operator. When a=b the integral is zero, so the zero-length interval case follows directly.

For time-independent fj in H^lambda and 0<=lambda<=1, ||C_I(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C_lambda |I|^lambda product_j||fj||_{H^lambda}; at |I|=0 the integral is zero. Constants are uniform in interval location and support, and the bounded interpretation agrees with smooth inputs.

argument.text:
For the product and stages use E003 with lambda=gamma and epsilon=1/8 at gamma=1/2. The diagonal bilinear stage is exactly F_n(t;w), by definition. The necessary source exponent checks and retained calculations are:
when \(\|w\|_{H^\gamma}\le M\). One can take \(a_\gamma=1/2-\gamma\) for \(0<\gamma<1/2\), \(1/8\) for \(\gamma=1/2\), and \(a_\gamma=0\) for \(\gamma>1/2\). For clarity, the source stage exponent is \(\theta=(1+\gamma-\beta)/(1+\gamma-\beta_0)\), with \(\beta_0=2\gamma-3/2\) for \(0<\gamma<1/2\), \(\beta_0=-1/2-\epsilon\) for \(\gamma=1/2\), and \(\beta_0=\gamma-1\) for \(1/2<\gamma\le1\). Take \(\epsilon=1/8\) in the middle case. At \(\beta=a_\gamma\) the exponents are respectively \((1/2+2\gamma)/(5/2-\gamma)\ge\gamma\), \(11/17>1/2\) and \((1+\gamma)/2\ge\gamma\). Every \(a_\gamma\) lies in the source interval \([\beta_0,1+\gamma]\). Since \(0<\tau\le1\), these exponents imply the first bound in the asserted stage inequalities. At \(\beta=1+\gamma\) the exponent is zero, giving the second. The product inequality is E003, with the same fixed \(1/8\) choice when \(\gamma=1/2\). Source \(L^2\) and \(H^s\) norms are \(\sqrt{2\pi}\) times ours; dividing the source inequalities absorbs only fixed factors into constants. These estimates require no regularity beyond \(H^\gamma\) on \(w\). For the first range the exponent inequality reduces to gamma^2-gamma/2+1/2=(gamma-1/4)^2+7/16>0; at gamma=1/2 the exponent is 11/17 and in the last range (1+gamma)/2>=gamma. Thus both stage conclusions follow uniformly for 0<tau<=1. All relevant bounds and the product inequality have now been proved in the declared normalization.

argument.text: H001,H002 give the original data and exponent conditions. Fix any real mean-zero g with ||g||_{H^gamma}<=R; all constants below are selected from N011 before this choice. Use u for its exact flow and u^n for its iterates, and set u_{0,m}=P_{<=m}g. Fourier cutoffs preserve reality and zero mean; ||u_{0,m}||_{H^gamma}<=R and ||u_{0,m}-g||_2->0 by summability of the Fourier norm. N001 gives the common exact-flow bound and sup_{[0,T]}||u_m-u||_2<=C(T,2R)||u_{0,m}-g||_2->0. N011 applies to every smooth u_{0,m} with the same C0,tau0.

produces.statement: u_{0,m} stay in the original ball, converge to g in L2, and sup_t||u_m-u||_2 tends to zero. There exist C0,tau0 depending only on T,gamma,R, the same for all m, such that for tau=T/L<=tau0 every smooth approximating flow and scheme obey max_{0<=n<=L}||u_m(n tau)-u_m^n||_2<=C0 tau^gamma.

argument.text: For each fixed tau>0 the unmodified Psi_tau is continuous L2->L2. N006 gives Dinv:L2->H^1 and the H^1 algebra bound, so F_tau:L2->H^1 is continuous quadratic. The first H_tau term is a product of inverse derivatives, hence continuous. The second uses the bilinear mean P0(f^2), bounded by ||f||_2^2, times S_tau Dinv f. In the third term each endpoint cube (S_s Dinv f)^3 is a continuous H^1 product followed by Dinv. In the fourth, S_{s-tau} Dinv2 F_tau(f) and S_s Dinv f are H^1 factors, followed by Dinv2. All coefficients, including 1/tau, are finite at fixed tau. The Airy terms are continuous by unitarity. Thus every displayed term is continuous into L2, and all iterates are well-defined; their formulas preserve reality and zero mean. For fixed positive L and tau=T/L finite induction gives u_m^n->u^n in L2 at every grid point.

produces.statement: For fixed tau>0, Psi_tau is continuous on L2 and preserves the real mean-zero class. On each fixed finite grid the approximating iterates converge to u^n in L2 at every grid point.

argument.text: Fix any positive L with tau=T/L<=tau0. Using F001,F002 pass to the limit in ||u_m(t_n)-u_m^n||_2<=C0 tau^gamma at every one of its L+1 grid points. Taking their finite maximum gives the output with the same constants. Since g was arbitrary this proves the whole-ball universal assertion, and H002 permits g=u0; C0,tau0 were selected using only T,gamma,R. Unitarity identifies physical and twisted errors. No spatial cutoff occurs in Psi; cutoffs appear only in this limiting argument. The solution class and approximation identification are those of N001. This proves the full target.
